corrected_statement: From a plan effective size (n_plan) of 300 a searched family adds a seeded scrambled-Sobol sample of 8 candidates (16 from 1,000; the forest capped at 8 by max_drawn; halved under 'lighter'; none under 'standard'/'manual') to the standard candidates, which come first and win ties; each is scored by the strictly proper primary pooled over K = 3 inner folds (or out of bag for an eligible forest) and the lowest loss is refit. RECIPES §4.2 chooses plain random search over halving/TPE for replay and a known budget, and cites random search as 'a surprisingly strong baseline' in low-effective-dimension spaces; S = 8/16 is a budget convention. The repo does not claim that this budget yields settings that predict at least as well as the standard settings on new data (it can only guarantee no worse on the inner loss, because the standard is a candidate).
source_note: RECIPES_AND_TUNING.md §4.2 'The strategy in v2' exists; reason 3 is the only methods reason (reasons 1-2 replay/budget, 4 halving dropped). Verified Bischl et al. 2023 (arXiv 2107.05847, §4.2.1): 'this makes RS preferable to GS and a surprisingly strong baseline for HPO in many practical settings'. Verified Bergstra & Bengio 2012 (JMLR 13) abstract: random trials more efficient than grid; 'only a few of the hyper-parameters really matter'. Neither source says 8 or 16 random candidates suffice to match or beat library defaults; they compare random search to grid search. The 8/16 sizes and 300/1,000 thresholds have no cited basis (conventions). In-repo evidence near the regime: notes/SMALL_SAMPLE_STANDARD.md §2 (nested 8 Sobol + standard beat the library defaults in all 14 simulated cells by 0.10-0.39 nats, but with the plan forced on below n_plan 300, S = 16 never studied; and a fixed conservative standard matched or beat the search in 5 of 8 family-cells at 1,000 rows).
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_rt5a_t1_nested_tuning.py::test_t1_flat_tuning_is_optimistic_and_nested_tuning_is_not (reports nested vs standard on fresh data but does not assert it; n = 200 with plan forced; scheduled-only). test_tuning_plan.py pins the counts, not accuracy.
note: The budget is a convention justified by a general literature statement about random vs grid search; nothing in the regime (n_plan >= 300, S = 16) checks that the chosen settings predict at least as well as the standard on fresh data. Present S as a convention. The 'cannot lose' guarantee holds only on the inner loss. Open item in RECIPES §4.6: whether the small-sample standard should join the search from 300.

corrected_statement: The signed paired difference between the fixed regression-with-splines benchmark (an additive model with every continuous predictor a restricted cubic spline, knots by Harrell's rule, no interactions and no penalty, fitted on the same folds; not fitted when the input count reaches n) and the flexible family that wins on the in-bag rows of each bootstrap resample of the first repeat's out-of-fold predictions (whole units together; BBC-CV over the flexible set), scored on the out-of-bag rows, estimates what the benchmark costs or gains on the strictly proper primary and, for numeric and yes/no outcomes only, on calibration (|1 - slope| of the flexible pick minus the benchmark's), with selection among the flexible families corrected; when the 95% percentile interval spans 0 the record says 'no measurable cost on these rows', an absence-of-evidence verdict.
source_note: Verified Rudin 2019 (Nat Mach Intell 1:206-215; ar5iv 1811.10154): 'It is a myth that there is necessarily a trade-off between accuracy and interpretability' and the 'artificial trade-off' sentence; this motivates the framing, not the estimator. Verified Tsamardinos et al. 2018 (Mach Learn; arXiv 1708.07180): BBC-CV bootstraps the pooled out-of-sample predictions, selects on the in-bag, estimates on the left-out rows, percentile intervals. The paper corrects the performance of a selected configuration; applying it to a paired difference against a fixed benchmark is the repo's extension (reasonable, not stated there). MODELING_SEQUENCE §5 asks for 'the best interpretable family' vs the best flexible, BBC-corrected; the code fixes the interpretable side to the spline benchmark (only the flexible side is chosen). 'Properly specified' is the review's phrase; the benchmark is a fixed additive spline model and is not guaranteed to be properly specified. |1 - slope| as the calibration distance is a convention.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_explore_5_shelf.py::test_6_the_cost_or_gain_is_bbc_corrected_over_the_flexible_set (an engine-free hand replay in explore_references.interpretable_bbc: it would fail if the pick were not re-made per resample, so it certifies the procedure, not the absence of optimism); ::test_6_through_the_stage_an_interaction_a_spline_regression_cannot_draw_costs_it (a known-truth sign check in an extreme case only). No test checks that the corrected difference is unbiased or that its interval covers.
note: The procedure matches BBC-CV as published and is checked by a hand replay. The no-optimism property for this paired difference rests on Tsamardinos by extension. Known caveats in the claim's notes stand: the P_OVER_N check counts inputs, not spline columns, so the benchmark can be non-unique and still fitted (e.g. p = n/3 with 5 knots), and a heavily overfit benchmark would then be misread as interpretability's cost. Calibration readout is skipped for multiclass/ordinal/time-to-event.

corrected_statement: Under prediction, Riley's minimum is computed only for a numeric or yes/no outcome (none for several classes, ordered classes or time to event: the shelf says it is not computed). Candidate predictor parameters count one per numeric predictor, k - 1 per category of k levels (text, or a column declared/confirmed as codes), every extra column a declared spline or quintile form adds, and, when Explore's spline rule or inner-CV form choice is on, k - 2 per bendable continuous predictor (numeric with at least MIN_DISTINCT values, not codes, no declared form), with k by Harrell's rule on the effective size (rows for a numeric or time-to-event outcome, the rarer class for yes/no, the smallest class for several classes). The yes/no criteria use the rarer class's share of the training rows. Under inference no Riley minimum is computed; the shelf's basis line and the SPV/EPV concerns count every analyzed row, and the rule's spline columns are not added.
source_note: Riley et al. BMJ 2020;368:m441 is not open (BMJ 403; Europe PMC not OA); the repo test quotes its worked examples. Verified the companion Riley et al. 2019 Stat Med Part II (PMC6519266): 'if a predictor is categorical with three of more categories, or continuous and modelled as a nonlinear trend, then including the predictor will require two or more parameters', and 'candidate' means 'considered, before any variable selection'. That supports k - 1 per category and counting spline columns. The k - 2 extra columns follow from the restricted cubic spline's k - 1 columns (Harrell). Effective size for knots on the rarer class is Harrell RMS §4.4 (cited in the test docstring). Counting the inner-CV candidates as splines is the app's conservative choice, consistent with 'before any variable selection'.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_explore_repair.py::test_5_rileys_minimum_counts_the_spline_rules_columns_among_the_candidate_parameters (hand-counted parameters 13/43/41 and Riley's criteria by hand; would fail if spline or category columns were miscounted); also test_wp8_inference_reporting.py::test_4c_the_shelf_counts_a_categorys_levels_as_parameters (pmsampsize, independent) and ::test_4a_rileys_minimum_matches_the_published_examples_and_pmsampsize.
note: The counting rule is sourced and the computation is checked against independent references. The statement overreaches only on scope: multiclass, ordinal and survival outcomes get no Riley minimum, and inference computes no Riley minimum at all. Riley's binary criteria use the outcome proportion, which the app takes from the training rows.

source_note: Internal: SURFACING_POLICY §2.4 sets the starting conventions (rows share x SMD >= 0.05 / >= 0.2) and §2.6 says how to calibrate them: on the twelve reference journeys, minimizing false reassurance at a cry-wolf budget, uncalibrated proxies capped at band 1. materiality.calibrate follows the 'zero false reassurance' half of that rule, but on 9 cases from one table (the NHANES fixture) through one simplified pipeline (complete cases, straight-line nutrients), not the reference journeys, and with no cry-wolf budget applied; the JSON's 'about' admits this. band_1 = 0.003697 is the m_pre of the smallest falsely reassured case (200-7,000 kcal: m_pre 0.003697, realized 0.20). Exactly one case lies below it (100-9,000 kcal: m_pre 0.0012, realized 0.011). It is a decision procedure with a methods reason (false reassurance is the costly error), not an external basis; Austin 2009 is cited only for the SMD itself. No source supports the general claim that M below 0.003697 implies movement below 0.1 half-width.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/test_materiality.py::test_the_committed_calibration_reassures_falsely_on_none_of_its_cases (in-sample: the threshold is set from these same cases so that this passes by construction). test_materiality_dietary_proof.py::test_a_narrow_screen_once_said_to_change_nothing_could_bias_and_is_upgraded_openly checks the post-lock relabel, not the threshold.
note: The app does say 'Doesn't change your numbers here' when M < 0.003697, on one in-sample band-0 case. The cases show the proxy does not rank movements: m_pre 0.0082 moved the estimate 0.41 half-widths while 0.185 (Goldberg) moved it 0.12, and 4 of the 8 band-1 predictions realized band 2, so the 0.2 'act on it' cut is never reached and under-alarms. 'calibrated: true' meets min_cases (5, a convention) but not §2.6's calibration set. The post-lock verify() relabels openly, which limits harm. Minor: the alternative is the rows the other rules keep without the screen, which is 'every row' only when the screen is the only exclusion.

source_note: Internal ruling only: MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 'Corrected' says 'A spline or categories on a residual breaks the identity with the standard model: it is the nutrient's curve on the energy-adjusted scale at mean energy, not the substitution curve. Its label changes, and spline(N) + E is offered as the route.' Its methods reason is that the identity (linear in N) does not survive a nonlinear basis. No external source is cited for the label (Willett, Howe & Kushi 1997 or Tomova et al. 2022 would be the natural ones). The code (residual_form, residual_label, substitution_route) matches the doc; the residual is N - N_hat(E) + N_hat(mean E), which supports the 'at mean energy' wording.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_form_8_energy_labels.py::test_8_a_residual_curves_label_and_route_are_the_reviews_words and test_form_1_order_and_invalidation.py::test_8_a_spline_on_a_residual_is_labeled_and_offers_the_substitution_route check the words and the route only. turbotab/core/tests/test_energy.py::test_residual_and_standard_models_give_the_same_nutrient_coefficient is an engine-independent OLS check of the straight-line identity (real for that half); nothing checks that the identity breaks under a spline or that spline(N) + E recovers a known substitution curve.
note: The straight-line identity is certified; the nonlinear half and the route rest on an internal methods ruling with a sound reason but no cited source or derivation. Nuance for the truth referees: under method 'residual' (energy kept), f(N - bE) + gE at fixed E is still a curve in N at that energy (one that shifts with E), so 'not the substitution curve at fixed total energy' is best read as 'not the standard model's single substitution curve'. The label also appears on the forms card for any residual nutrient before a nonlinear form is chosen (exposure_form.py:1443), which is informative rather than wrong.

corrected_statement: In a declared parallel or cluster-randomized trial the recommended analysis set is intention to treat: everyone randomized, in the arm they were randomized to, whatever they received or did afterwards (crossovers stay in their randomized arm). The primary analysis then fits only those in the set with an observed outcome, assuming missing outcomes are missing at random given arm and covariates (stated in the notice), with a delta-adjusted tipping-point analysis that imputes every missing outcome as the sensitivity analysis (White, Horton, Carpenter & Pocock 2011's strategy). Randomization protects the comparison, and the effect estimated is that of being assigned. Trial designs are 'Not available yet' in the interview (designs.py), so this engine core is not yet reachable by a user.
source_note: Verified White, Horton, Carpenter & Pocock 2011 (BMJ 342:d40; PMC3230114): ITT means 'all participants ... included in the analysis in the groups to which they were randomised, regardless of any departures from randomised treatment'. Its strategy is to 'Perform a main analysis of all observed data that are valid under a plausible assumption about the missing data' and to 'Account for all randomised participants, at least in the sensitivity analyses'. The app's observed-outcome primary analysis plus tipping point matches this. Checked CONSORT 2010 E&E (Moher et al. 2010, BMJ 340:c869; PMC2844943) item 16: ITT is preferred, and the effect of assignment differs from the effect of receipt. Item 16 itself is a reporting item ('whether the analysis was by original assigned groups'); the preference is in the E&E text.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_e2_trials.py::test_intention_to_treat_keeps_everyone_randomized_as_randomized_and_per_protocol_the_adherent (a hand check that the set is everyone randomized and crossovers stay; it would fail if the set definition changed, but nothing checks the interpretive part, e.g. a simulation with non-adherence showing the ITT estimate recovers the assignment effect). Estimator tests (test_ancova_matches_lm_and_emmeans, beeca, pbkrtest, gee) are R references for the estimators, not for ITT.
note: A standard, well-sourced principle; the set definition is checked by hand. The statement overstates by implying everyone randomized is analyzed: rows with no outcome are left out of the primary fit under MAR (S4-097), which is the White et al. strategy and is disclosed in the notice. Not reachable yet: parallel_trial and cluster_randomized_trial are NOT_YET in designs.py.

corrected_statement: Under prediction a named grouping is recorded without intercepts: a set_clusters answer with fixed-effects or cluster-only adjustment is refused (code not_inference), with the grouping alone as its exit. The grouping then names the cluster for the split question's internal-external validation option (folds = the groups, if the user picks it), and evaluation runs leave-one-cluster-out internal-external cross-validation, reporting each cluster and the spread. The ordinary k-fold folds and the held-out rows are grouped by the grain's identifier, not by this cluster, unless internal-external validation is chosen.
source_note: Internal: audit RO-08 (AUDIT_REPORT.md:637) recommends 'Under prediction: offer internal-external (leave-one-cluster-out) validation and grouped folds'. MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 'Repeated units or clusters ... imply, under prediction: grouped folds and a grouped holdout, a bootstrap by unit, and performance heterogeneity across sites'. Both give a decision; neither gives a methods reason for refusing intercepts under prediction. Verified Collins et al. 2024 (BMJ 384:e074819; PMC10772854) Box 4: 'Internal-external validation exploits a common feature present in many datasets, namely that of clustering', and it lets 'the generalisability and heterogeneity of performance' be examined across clusters. It does not discuss cluster fixed effects or intercepts in a prediction model. So the source supports the validation half; the refusal is the app's ruling.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_wp17_purpose_routes.py::test_4_under_prediction_the_grouping_names_internal_external_validation (pins the refusal and that the IE option carries the cluster: behavior, not the methods premise); test_wp9_validation_performance.py::test_6_internal_external_validation_reports_each_cluster_and_the_spread covers the IECV computation.
note: The refusal is defensible for transport to new sites (a new site's intercept is unknown), but site intercepts are a legitimate choice when the model is used only at the known sites, so this is a convention the app has chosen, not a rule. 'Whole groups kept together' is overstated: MODELING_SEQUENCE's grouped folds and grouped holdout by cluster are not what the code does by default; only IECV and the opt-in internal_external folds use the cluster.

source_note: The code cites nothing (IOM 2000 is cited a few lines up for the EAR only). Internal basis found that the inventory missed: NUTRITION_PACK.md §E (line 753), under rules marked [SETTLED]: 'The UL side: report % above the UL only for total intake including supplements', with no line-level citation (the pack has no IOM 2000 / DRI Applications citation). The rule is the IOM DRI framing (the UL refers to total intake from food, water and supplements), but it has nutrient exceptions. The IOM ULs for magnesium cover non-food (pharmacological/supplement) sources only; folate, niacin and vitamin E cover synthetic forms from supplements and fortified foods. Partly verified: an open EFSA-based study (Eur J Nutr 2023, PMC10421806) footnotes 'The UL applies to supplements only' for folic acid, magnesium and vitamin E. The IOM primary text could not be fetched (NCBI captcha; ODS 403).
test_judged: None found: no test references the UL sentence (grep for 'share above the UL' and '"UL"' in tests finds nothing).
note: The app always prints this conditional; it never asks whether the recalls include supplements. Gloss for the truth referees: 'since the UL applies to total intake' is wrong for magnesium, where food-only intake above the UL is not a risk, and for folate, niacin and vitamin E, where the UL concerns synthetic forms. For those nutrients the sentence should name the form the UL covers. The UL wording needs a nutrient-specific source (IOM 2000/2006 DRI tables).

corrected_statement: Under complete cases, the 'No predictor missing' step drops a row only for a blank in a predictor that is settled (its role confirmed by the user or corroborated by its values at high confidence; BLUEPRINT §14.1) and kept: not left out by the missing-values answer, a repair marking it unusable, or, under inference, the adjustment answers. When the categorical answer is 'missing_category', blanks in categorical or two-valued predictors are a 'Missing' level and drop no row (numeric columns cannot take that level). A role that rode along unsettled drops no row, and the fit asks for its confirmation first.
source_note: Internal only. BLUEPRINT §14.1 exists and says 'Every number-changing consumer reads only settled readings', where settled means 'its values corroborate it at high confidence or the user confirmed it'. So it supports the settled-roles rule, as an architectural ruling (the leash), not a missing-data methods reason. SetMissing.categorical == 'missing_category' is a code fact (pipeline.level_columns, rows.cohort_inputs). No methods source is cited for treating blanks-as-a-level as values; the literature the inventory names (Greenland & Finkle 1995; Groenwold et al. 2012) cautions that the missing-indicator method biases adjusted estimates unless the missingness is structural (skip patterns).
test_judged: None targets the rule. turbotab/server/tests/test_previews.py::test_recorded_sentences_count_rows_as_the_participant_flow_does checks that the sentence matches the flow's own count (self-consistency). test_skip_pattern_blanks.py tests which fill is recommended, not which rows complete cases drop. No test shows that a Missing-level column or an unsettled role drops no row.
note: The code does what the statement says, with two refinements: 'confirmed' means settled (which includes high-confidence readings), and 'kept' also excludes repair-unusable and adjustment-left-out columns. Row accounting is cheap to certify by hand (a frame with a blank in a Missing-level column, an unsettled role and a settled numeric predictor). Methods pairing for the truth referees: keeping blank-as-level rows is sound for structural skip-pattern blanks, but under inference it is the missing-indicator method for other blanks.

source_note: Verified all three quotes. NIAAA ('What Is a Standard Drink?'): 'in the United States, one standard drink contains about 14 grams, or about 0.6 fluid ounces, of pure alcohol'. NHS ('Calculating alcohol units'): 'One unit equals 10ml or 8g of pure alcohol'. Kalinowski & Humphreys 2016 (Addiction 111:1293-1298, via Europe PMC): 'the modal standard drink size was 10 g pure ethanol, but variation was wide (8-20 g)' among 37 countries. The 7 kcal/g for alcohol is the general Atwater factor (NUTRITION_PACK §01; energy._FALLBACK_ATWATER).
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_ledger_repair_3.py::test_a2_a_carbohydrate_to_alcohol_swap_asks_alcohols_unit_and_moves_drinks_at_98_kcal (an engine-free NumPy OLS at 98 kcal a drink; it would fail if the app moved drinks at 7 kcal a unit). test_ledger_repair_2.py (~line 712) checks that drinks:7.99 and drinks:20.01 are rejected. Both check the arithmetic and the bounds; the constants are inputs, so their truth rests on the sources.
note: The constants are verified against primary sources and the conversion is checked independently. The grade is 'sourced' rather than 'certified' only because the tests take 14 g and 7 kcal/g as given. The app never infers the drink size from the values; the user's recorded unit settles it.

source_note: There is no basis beyond the docstring of materiality.collinear_label ('Under Predict the pair scan's lever (a penalty in each fold) is a decision: Decide') and the crosswalk ceiling ('Decide, right under Predict', quest.EXPLORE_FINDINGS). No methods reason is given for why collinearity matters to predictive performance. The repo's own Predict design contradicts the code: calm/BEATS_PREDICT.md M4 'Set for you' treats near-collinear body measures as a convention the user confirms ('the four body measures, which carry nearly one quantity, are all kept and read together'; 'near-collinear predictors; grouped importance'; 'Confirm all 4'), not as a Decide. The pair threshold |r| >= 0.90 is labeled a convention (explore.COLLINEAR).
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/test_collinear_adjustment.py::test_the_collinear_line_is_decide_only_where_what_you_study_is_in_it (its last assertion pins Decide under prediction; it pins the policy, not any methods premise).
note: The code does what the claim says. But no basis is given, and the policy contradicts the repo's own Predict beats, which present collinear predictors as a confirmed convention with grouped importance. It also cuts against the materiality framework elsewhere (Decide regardless of materiality), and against the methods point that collinearity rarely harms prediction and that regularization is already a family choice. Send to the orchestrator to reconcile with BEATS_PREDICT M4 (likely Confirm or For the record under Predict, with grouped importance in Results).

source_note: Internal: NUTRITION_PACK §04 Coaching (line 525) carries this exact text, marked '[DISPUTED — the app must not pick a side]', and the §04 Diagnostic says to detect weight, BMI, adiposity and diabetes outcomes and 'escalate the mediation/collider warning'. The pack gives no line-level primary source for it. dietary_caveats.py cites Tomova et al. 2022 (AJCN 115:189; PMC8755101). Verified there: total energy as a collider of its components ('conditioning on the collider ... creates a dependency between all the constituent components'; 'Adjusting for TE ... opens conditional dependencies between the exposure and all competing energy sources'). Tomova's collider is a different mechanism from the adiposity-driven under-reporting this claim names, and the paper says nothing about adiposity, under-reporting or presenting both models. So the statement rests on the pack's DISPUTED ruling, with no verified source for the under-reporting and mediator argument.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_wp15_claims.py::test_3_an_energy_related_outcome_pushes_the_disputed_note_onto_the_energy_card and ::test_3_energy_related_outcomes_are_read_by_whole_tokens (the trigger and the badge or text appearing; nothing about the causal claim, e.g. a simulation where adjusting for reported energy biases a known diet-adiposity effect).
note: The app already labels this DISPUTED and recommends presenting both models, which suits its grade. It should cite primary sources for the two mechanisms: adiposity-related energy under-reporting (e.g. the doubly labelled water literature) and energy as a mediator. Tomova 2022 is cited nearby but supports a different collider argument. As the inventory notes, diabetes is in the trigger list, but the causal argument is stated only for adiposity.

source_note: The DESIGN card's 'why' (content.py:404-407) cites nothing; the drawer cites STROBE-nut only for naming the design. The trial half matches the engine core's own sourced docstring (methods/trials.py: adjustment 'for precision only', randomization factors per Kahan & Morris 2012, ANCOVA per Vickers & Altman 2001, binary effects standardized to marginal risks per Ye et al. 2023). Because the app standardizes, its trial estimand stays marginal, which makes 'precision only' true of the app's own trial analysis even for yes/no outcomes. The case-control, matched-set and observational sentences have no cited basis here. They are textbook conventions (e.g. Rothman, Greenland & Lash; Breslow & Day), not verified in this pass.
test_judged: None for the card's sentences. test_e2_trials.py::test_causal_wording_only_for_intention_to_treat_and_per_protocol_never_alone and ::test_the_adjustment_is_exactly_the_named_terms_and_nothing_is_selected check the trial core's behavior, not this explanatory text, and the trial designs are 'Not available yet' (designs.py).
note: Three overstatements: (1) 'only sharpens precision' holds for marginal (standardized) estimands; for conditional odds or hazard ratios adjustment changes the estimand, as the app's own 'non-collapsible' term says (content.py:1393). (2) A case-control sample can give absolute risk when the sampling fractions are known (population-based or nested designs). (3) 'Speaks of associations' is a reporting convention, not a methods necessity. Suggested wording: '... adjustment is for precision, not confounding; a case-control sample cannot give prevalence or absolute risk without the sampling fractions; ...'. Explanatory only for now, since trials, case-control and matched designs are Not available yet.

corrected_statement: Under inference, a site that differs in both the exposure and the outcome confounds the estimate, and intervals that treat its participants as independent can be too narrow. The grouping question therefore offers, first, an intercept per site with CR2 cluster-robust intervals on Bell-McCaffrey degrees of freedom (the small-sample correction few clusters need), or cluster-robust intervals only, which leave between-site differences in the estimate. 'Nothing groups them' over a column that reads as a grouping must be recorded with a reason. Under prediction the grouping carries no intercepts; it drives leave-one-cluster-out internal-external validation and names the cluster for the internal-external fold option. The ordinary folds and the held-out rows keep each participant's rows together, not each site's.
source_note: The card cites nothing for this text (its drawer cites NUTRITION_PACK §08 for split hygiene by participant). Internal rulings: audit RO-08 ('Under inference: adjust and cluster, or record why not. Under prediction: offer internal-external (leave-one-cluster-out) validation and grouped folds'), with a known-truth demonstration: within-site sodium effect 0; app 0.76-0.90 naive; site fixed effects -0.04 to -0.08. MODELING_SEQUENCE §2: 'cluster-aware intervals ... and a small-sample sandwich (CR2, Bell-McCaffrey df) with refusal below a floor'. models/inference.py cites Bell & McCaffrey 2002 and Cameron & Miller for the few-cluster correction (not re-fetched here). Collins et al. 2024 Box 4 (verified, see B-373) supports internal-external validation under prediction.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_wp17_purpose_routes.py::test_4_a_cluster_question_fires_and_site_fixed_effects_reproduce_the_audit (the audit's confounded multi-site fixtures with true within-site effect 0, through the real API; the estimate must equal statsmodels OLS with C(site) to 1e-8 and match the audit's -0.04/-0.08, near the truth, against about 0.8 without intercepts; the interval must equal CR2 with Bell-McCaffrey df written out by definition, and be wider than z). It would fail if the site intercepts or the small-sample correction were missing. It does not check that independence intervals are too narrow, or the prediction half.
note: Certified for the inference action (site intercepts remove site-level confounding on a known-truth fixture; CR2 against an independent reference). 'Too narrow' holds when both the exposure and the residuals are correlated within sites (the Moulton factor); it is not universal. As the inventory notes, site intercepts remove only site-level confounding. The prediction clause overstates grouping: only internal-external validation keeps sites together (see B-373). In the 10-site fixture the audit's z interval excludes the true 0, and the test asserts only that CR2 is wider, not that it covers 0.

corrected_statement: The engine asks the energy question under Predict. Under the dietary lens, with an energy column and an exposure, the Router's energy_adjustment question is open under prediction (interview._energy_applicability has no purpose gate; test_interview.py::test_energy_adjustment_applies_under_the_dietary_lens_only asserts status 'open' with purpose='prediction'), and the substitution question is likewise gated only by energy-bearing exposures. Under prediction the energy options are ranked so that every method keeping total energy comes before every method dropping it, and the energy-dropped residual is labeled unsound because it 'discards total energy's signal' (test_wp17_purpose_routes.py::test_5). The energy finding's text adds 'For prediction, models that keep total energy predict alike' (dietary_caveats.ENERGY_WHY). BEATS_PREDICT §9 ruling 5 ('neither is asked'; nutrients enter as recorded beside total calories, For the record) is a design ruling the engine does not yet implement.
source_note: BEATS_PREDICT.md §9 ruling 5 (line ~1169) exists. Its methods reason: the energy model decides what a coefficient means, which is an Estimate question (Willett, Howe & Kushi 1997), and a substitution compares two imagined diets, an effect (Shmueli 2010). Those sources support the explain-versus-predict distinction, not the user-facing 'models that keep total energy predict alike'.
